scenery.name: Statue of Liberty
scenery.location: New York Harbor, New York City, USA
scenery.description: A colossal neoclassical statue gifted by France, symbolizing freedom and democracy.

scenery.name: Golden Gate Bridge
scenery.description: An iconic red suspension bridge spanning the Golden Gate Strait, often shrouded in fog.

scenery.name: Yellowstone National Park
scenery.description: The first U.S. national park, famous for geysers, hot springs, and abundant wildlife.

scenery.name: Las Vegas Strip
scenery.description: A dazzling stretch of resorts, casinos, and neon lights that never sleeps.

scenery.name: Grand Canyon National Park
scenery.description: A breathtaking canyon carved by the Colorado River, showcasing layered red rock cliffs.

scenery.name: Eiffel Tower
scenery.description: A wrought-iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars, one of the most recognizable structures in the world.

scenery.name: Notre-Dame de Paris
scenery.location: Île de la Cité, Paris, France
scenery.description: A Gothic masterpiece and cathedral known for its stunning architecture, rose windows, and historical significance.

scenery.name: The Louvre
scenery.description: The world’s largest art museum, housing iconic works such as the Mona Lisa and Venus de Milo.

scenery.name: Arc de Triomphe
scenery.location: Place Charles de Gaulle, Paris, France
scenery.description: A triumphal arch honoring those who fought and died for France, offering panoramic views of the city.

scenery.name: Mont Blanc
scenery.location: Alps, border of France and Italy
scenery.description: The highest mountain in the Alps, renowned for its majestic snow-capped peaks and mountaineering routes.

scenery.name: Giza Pyramid
scenery.description: The monumental pyramids of Giza, ancient tombs built for pharaohs and one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

scenery.name: Great Sphinx
scenery.description: A limestone statue with a lion’s body and a human head, symbolizing royal power and wisdom.

scenery.name: Nile River
scenery.location: Flowing through northeastern Africa, primarily Egypt and Sudan
scenery.description: The world’s longest river, vital to Egypt’s history and civilization, supporting agriculture and life for millennia.

scenery.name: Abu Simbel
scenery.description: Twin temples carved into rock cliffs, built by Pharaoh Ramses II and relocated to save them from flooding.

scenery.name: Sahara Desert
scenery.location: Northern Africa, covering much of Egypt’s western territory
scenery.description: The largest hot desert in the world, featuring vast sand dunes, oases, and ancient caravan routes.

scenery.name: Big Ben
scenery.description: The iconic clock tower at the north end of the Palace of Westminster, symbolizing British heritage.

scenery.name: Stonehenge
scenery.description: A prehistoric stone monument of mysterious origins, believed to be used for ceremonial or astronomical purposes.

scenery.name: Lake District
scenery.description: A mountainous region known for its lakes, forests, and literary associations, designated as a UNESCO World Heritage site.

scenery.name: Tower of London
scenery.description: A historic castle on the River Thames, known for housing the Crown Jewels and its royal history.

scenery.name: Tower Bridge
scenery.description: A combined bascule and suspension bridge, one of London’s most famous landmarks over the River Thames.

scenery.name: Tokyo Skytree
scenery.description: A broadcasting and observation tower, the tallest structure in Japan, offering panoramic views of Tokyo.

scenery.name: Osaka Castle
scenery.description: A historic castle surrounded by moats and parks, symbolizing Japan’s feudal past and architectural elegance.

scenery.name: Fuji Mountain
scenery.description: Japan’s highest peak, a perfectly symmetrical volcano revered as a sacred symbol of beauty and inspiration.

scenery.name: Kiyomizu-dera
scenery.description: A famous Buddhist temple known for its wooden stage overlooking cherry and maple trees, and Kyoto cityscape.

scenery.name: Itsukushima Shrine
scenery.description: A UNESCO World Heritage Shinto shrine famous for its ‘floating’ torii gate rising from the sea.
